short-stories.title: A Rainy Morning
short-stories.story: Maya woke up to the sound of rain tapping on her window. She had planned to go jogging, but the weather changed her mind. Instead, she made tea and opened her grammar book. For an hour she practiced past perfect sentences. When the sun finally appeared, she felt ready for the day.

short-stories.title: The Job Interview
short-stories.story: Arjun had prepared for weeks. He had reviewed common interview questions and practiced answers in front of a mirror. On the day of the interview, he arrived early. While he was waiting, he noticed he was feeling calm. The interviewer smiled and said, 'Tell me about a time you solved a difficult problem.'

sentence-reading.text: Present simple: Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius.
Present continuous: She is working on her thesis this semester.
Past simple: They visited Rome last summer.
Past continuous: I was cooking dinner when the guests arrived.
Present perfect: We have lived here since 2019.
Past perfect: He had forgotten his keys before he reached the door.
Future simple: The train will depart at six o'clock.
Future continuous: This time next week, they will be travelling abroad.

passage-comprehension.passage: Language learners often confuse present perfect and past simple. Present perfect connects the past to now: 'I have finished my homework.' Past simple describes a finished time: 'I finished my homework at five o'clock.' When you see words like 'yesterday' or 'last year', use past simple. When you see 'already', 'yet', or 'since', think present perfect.

questions.q: Which sentence uses present perfect correctly?
Past simple is best when the time is:

passage-comprehension.passage: Future forms in English include 'will' for decisions and predictions, 'going to' for plans, and present continuous for fixed arrangements. 'I will help you' suggests a spontaneous offer. 'I am going to study abroad' shows a plan. 'We are meeting the client on Tuesday' is a scheduled arrangement.

questions.q: 'We are meeting the client on Tuesday' expresses:

grammar.q: She ___ to the gym every Tuesday.
grammar.explain: Present simple with third-person singular takes -s.
Past continuous for an action in progress when another action happened.

grammar.q: I ___ this book three times already.
grammar.explain: Present perfect with 'already' for life experience up to now.

grammar.q: By next month, she ___ here for ten years.
grammar.explain: Future perfect for duration completed before a future point.

grammar.q: He ___ his keys before he left the house.
grammar.explain: Past perfect for an earlier past action.
Present continuous for a planned future arrangement.

grammar.q: At eight o'clock tonight, I ___ TV.
grammar.explain: Future continuous for an action in progress at a future time.
Present perfect with 'since' for an action starting in the past and continuing.

story-retelling.title: The Late Train
story-retelling.story: Sara had packed her bag the night before. She set two alarms but still overslept. While she was rushing to the station, she realised she had forgotten her ticket. A kind stranger let her use a phone. She called her office and explained she would be late. The train had already left, so she took a taxi instead.

story-retelling.title: Learning to Cook
story-retelling.story: David had never cooked before he moved out of his parents' home. At first he burned toast and overcooked pasta. He watched videos every evening and practiced on weekends. After three months he was making full meals. His friends were surprised when he invited them to dinner last Friday.
